mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a strictly accelerating week-on-week recovery (-72.6, -67.3, -57.6, -41.1) over the last four weeks, indicating positive momentum in retail reopening that should persist as consumer confidence and store operating hours continue normalizing, pushing the next-4-week mean higher.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weeks of narrowing RETAIL_REC deficit
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, despite the prior four-week monotonic improvement trend, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (24.3 to 12.7) signals households spending less time confined at home, which behaviorally frees up discretionary time for shopping and dining trips, raising RETAIL_REC once RESIDENTIAL falls below a 15-point threshold.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dropped from 24.3 to 12.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its prior-28-day mean, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility jointly captures restored commuting patterns; when both series rise together, the combined effect of transit-enabled access and daytime workplace presence compounds to lift retail footfall more than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -69.0 to -39.9 and WORKPLACES from -64.0 to -40.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue rising over the next 4 weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean does not increase relative to the prior period, the interaction mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp acceleration in GROCERY_PHARM recovery (-48.0 to -8.4) reflects easing of public health restrictions on essential and non-essential retail alike; since grocery/pharmacy categories are typically first to normalize under policy relaxation, this leading indicator implies retail and recreation venues will follow with a lag as restrictions broaden.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 15 points within two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 20.5 points in the most recent week alone
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 15 points within two weeks but RETAIL_REC's subsequent 4-week mean does not rise relative to the prior 4-week mean, the leading-indicator hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Entering mid-June in Hong Kong, rising PARKS mobility (-68.4 to -46.1) reflects seasonal preference for outdoor recreation during warmer months; this substitution effect diverts discretionary leisure time away from indoor retail and recreation venues, dampening RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved steadily each week from -68.4 to -46.1
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility continues rising over the next 4 weeks and RETAIL_REC's mean also rises rather than falls relative to the prior period, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week jump in TRANSIT mobility exceeding 10 points signals an abrupt surge in people moving through the city, which within one week directly translates into higher retail and recreation footfall as transit hubs feed nearby shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 15.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises more than 10 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not show a positive mean shift in the following week, the short-horizon threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse co-movement of WORKPLACES rising and RESIDENTIAL falling jointly indicates a policy-driven shift away from stay-home mandates toward office and in-person economic activity; this combined signal, stronger than either series alone, predicts retail recovery as commuting and reduced home-confinement compound.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -64.0 to -40.6 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.3 to 12.7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues rising and RESIDENTIAL continues falling together but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean does not exceed the prior period's mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility recovers systematically one to two weeks ahead of RETAIL_REC in the snapshot, consistent with essential retail leading broader discretionary retail reopening; this lead-lag pattern should persist, producing a positive shift in RETAIL_REC within the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM gap to baseline narrowed faster than RETAIL_REC each of the last four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to lead in recovery magnitude but RETAIL_REC's mean over the next week does not rise relative to the current week, the lead-lag hypothesis is rejected.
